issues.claim: But the compiler must guarantee that the called method does not change an instance passed by `in`. If the struct is mutable, it cannot prove that a method leaves it unchanged, so it copies the struct before the call.
issues.problem: This describes the mechanism wrongly. The caller does not copy the struct before passing it by `in`; that would cancel the benefit of `in`. The defensive copy happens inside the callee. It happens each time a non-`readonly` member is invoked on the `in` parameter of a non-readonly struct, because the compiler cannot prove that member leaves the struct unchanged. Answer item 4 states this correctly, so the explanation contradicts the answer and teaches a wrong model.
issues.suggestedFix: Rewrite the paragraph: `in` and `ref readonly` pass an address, so the call itself does not copy. Inside the method the parameter is read-only, so when you call a member that is not marked `readonly` on an `in` parameter of a non-readonly struct, the compiler cannot prove the member leaves the struct unchanged. It therefore copies the struct to a temporary and calls the member on that copy. Each such member call can copy again. A `readonly struct`, or `readonly` members, tells the compiler no copy is needed. Apply the same change in RU: 'при вызове внутри метода члена, не помеченного readonly, у `in`-параметра изменяемой структуры компилятор копирует структуру во временную переменную и вызывает член у копии'.

issues.problem: The fetched excerpts of the cited pages show that `in` avoids the copy cost and that passing large structs by value is expensive. They do not show the defensive-copy behaviour. The struct page only lists 'Readonly structs' and 'Readonly instance members' as spec clauses. The method-parameters excerpt is truncated and does not show support. The claim is true, but no cited page demonstrably supports it. The linkTitle 'Параметры методов: ref, in, ref readonly, out' is also not the page's real title ('Method parameters and modifiers').
issues.suggestedFix: Add the link https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/write-safe-efficient-code (kind docs, lang en), which covers `in`, `readonly struct` and defensive copies, and add a matching linkTitle in both locales. Alternatively cite the 'readonly instance members' section of the struct docs. Align the link title with the real page title.
